name: Zenkit
tagline: Projects, tasks, wikis, and database-style views across a product suite

tiers.limits: Maximum 10 users; 100 workspaces; 50 lists; 20,000 items; 1,000 comments/seat/month; 300 automation runs/seat/month; 6 GB storage.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (save up to 16%); exact monthly prices were not exposed by the live static page; 14-day trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every organization member, including owners and admins, is billable on paid plans; VAT is excluded; quota overages have a roughly 14-day grace period before restrictions; the post-trial account can become export-only.

verdictSummary: Zenkit's solo core is compact: build a single-user flexible work management workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on collaboration, integrations, polish.
coreLoopDIY: Build a single-user flexible work management workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
whyPeopleStillPay: Zenkit: Teams pay because shared state, notifications, permissions, and migrations are harder than the visible board or list.
ongoingBurden: Maintain notifications, recurring-date logic, importers, permissions, backups, and collaboration conflict handling.

priorArt.name: Vikunja
priorArt.desc: Open-source task manager with lists, boards, and collaboration.

rejectedAlternatives.name: AFFiNE
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Documents, whiteboards, and databases are real; there is no mature project-task engine

rejectedAlternatives.name: AppFlowy
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The workspace has databases and kanban, but free self-hosted collaboration is one member plus guests

rejectedAlternatives.name: Docmost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The open-source wiki is real, but the database and kanban feature called Bases is commercial

notes: Strong page because Zenkit separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Zenkit.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a single-user flexible work management workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: enterprise permissions; large integration catalog; mobile capture and notifications.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
